title: spec review: S3a evidence reuse from cancelled or failed workers: partial results become evidence objects with provenance worker_partial, routed to the replacement worker (P27)
spec:
orchestrator/evidence.py: add provenance value worker_partial to PROVENANCE (trust_class LOCAL_USER, trust field untrusted stays as for non-repo provenance, scan applied as for any evidence). orchestrator/worker_control.py: after cancel builds the partial result, and in a new hook worker_control.preserve_partial(task) that daemon.reconcile_dead calls for a dead worker with a dirty worktree, create evidence objects in the goal's evidence pool (evidence.make with source_type worker_partial, location the task id plus the worktree head sha, content = the partial facts rendered as compact lines: files changed with diff stat, commits with subjects, tests run and their result lines, error tail, files inspected; commit = worktree head sha; freshness by the existing hash mechanism). Replacement routing: orchestrator/context_router.py treats worker_partial evidence whose location task shares the same goal and overlaps the current task's scope (write or read) as high relevance (never HIDE) with a cap of [context_router].partial_max_tokens (default 800, dated comment); orchestrator/spawn.py renders those items under a packet section prior_worker (after evidence) with the source task id and the head sha, so the new worker can check out or diff it instead of rediscovering; the section is empty when nothing applies. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/16-evidence-reuse.md.
Spec review T-1198 folded in: (1) evidence.py: add worker_partial to BOTH SOURCE_TYPES and PROVENANCE (make() validates each separately) and add an explicit entry worker_partial -> LOCAL_USER in the _trust_class dict, documenting in the module docstring that LOCAL_USER covers locally produced artifacts (memory and observed worker outputs), not only user-authored memory. (2) fresh() and context_router's duplicate/staleness check are extended so worker_partial evidence goes stale when its commit differs from the goal head (same commit == head_sha rule as source_chunk and test_result). (3) Shadow-first: the prior_worker section is rendered only when [context_router].mode is active; in shadow the would-be section (ids and chars) is logged on the context_route decision row and the packet is unchanged. (4) preserve_partial is idempotent: it stamps pipeline.partial_preserved_at on the task and returns early when the stamp exists, so reconcile_dead re-runs every tick without growing the pool. (5) Overlap is computed from persisted data only: the dead task's write scope against the current task's write scope plus its packet-time read scope; no read footprint of the dead task is stored. (6) tests/test_worker_control.py exists with class WorkerControl; add the new test as a method there.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.
acceptance: tests/test_worker_control.py::test_cancel_and_preserve_partial_create_evidence_objects (pool contains the facts with commit sha; no prompt or transcript text)

risks.issue: Evidence carries no scope field, and route()/_choice() only receive the current task, not the dead task's task record. relevance_for's scope_match compares `_location_path(location)` (a real file path) against the current task's scope — for worker_partial the location is `task_id:head_sha`, which will never path-match anything, so the existing relevance machinery cannot express 'dead task's write scope overlaps current task's scope'. The spec never states how context_router obtains the dead task's write scope: bus.py (which owns task records) is not in scope, and no new Evidence field for scope is specified. Without that, test_context_router.py::test_worker_partial_evidence_never_hidden_for_overlapping_scope_and_capped has no defined fixture shape.

The main spec says worker_partial evidence for overlapping scope is 'high relevance (never HIDE)', but folded-in item (2) extends the staleness rule at line 83-85 (`if head_sha is not None and not evidence.fresh(ev, head_sha) and ev.source_type in (...) : return HIDE, stale`) to also cover worker_partial. Since (2) requires adding worker_partial to that source_type tuple for staleness to work, a stale-but-overlapping worker_partial item would be HIDden, directly contradicting the 'never HIDE' clause. Spec doesn't say which rule wins.

'[context_router].partial_max_tokens (default 800)' has no expression in the current HIDE/SHORT/LONG/FULL level model — there is no per-item token/byte cap anywhere in _choice()/_text()/route(). The spec doesn't say whether the cap is enforced by picking a lower LEVEL, by truncating content at evidence-creation time in worker_control.preserve_partial (mirroring the existing _bounded_result trim loop in worker_control.cancel), or by a new render path in context_router. Left unspecified, acceptance test test_context_router.py::test_worker_partial_evidence_never_hidden_for_overlapping_scope_and_capped has no defined truncation boundary to assert against.

PROVENANCE currently drives _trust_class via a 2-entry dict defaulting everything else to EXTERNAL; the folded-in note (1) correctly calls for an explicit worker_partial->LOCAL_USER entry, but SOURCE_TYPES has no worker_partial value at all yet — make() will raise ValueError('invalid source_type') until both SOURCE_TYPES and PROVENANCE are updated together. Spec covers this but worth pinning as a single-commit requirement so a partial edit (only PROVENANCE, not SOURCE_TYPES, or vice versa) doesn't pass review.

suggested_spec_changes: Specify exactly how context_router.py learns the dead task's write scope for overlap detection: either (a) worker_control.preserve_partial snapshots the dead task's scope list into a new Evidence.relevance key (e.g. relevance['source_scope']) at creation time via evidence.make(task=dead_task), and context_router._choice compares that snapshot against the current task's scope+read_scope, with no bus.py dependency; or (b) explicitly add orchestrator/bus.py to scope for a bus.get(source_task_id) lookup. Pick one and name the exact field/call.

State precedence between the 'never HIDE for overlapping scope' rule and the staleness-HIDE rule added in folded-in item (2): does a stale-but-overlapping worker_partial item get HIDden or shown at a capped level anyway?

State where the partial_max_tokens cap is enforced (worker_control.preserve_partial content truncation vs. a new context_router render path) and what happens to the trimmed content (which lines drop first), analogous to the existing _bounded_result trim order in worker_control.cancel.
